A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Simple Policy Optimization and contain complete, readable main text and appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v8 reports original Atari and MuJoCo experiments, including algorithm comparisons, network-depth studies, and learning curves in the appendices.

after.justification: v9 retains original MuJoCo and Atari results and reports a broader ResNet-18 Atari comparison in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The SPO objective, losses, update procedure, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. ResNet-18 already appears in v8; its expanded evaluation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Figure 10 expands Atari coverage from 40 to 54 distinct games, retaining the original games and adding 14 previously unreported tasks, including Atlantis, Carnival, MontezumaRevenge, and Pitfall. This substantially broadens Atari task coverage; MuJoCo coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The MuJoCo comparators remain PPO-Clip, PPO-Penalty, SPU, PPO-RB, TR-PPO, TR-PPO-RB, and RPO. Figure 10 retains the PPO-versus-SPO comparison; its encoder changes concern experimental settings.

E3.justification: Figure 10 replaces the earlier 10-million-step Atari comparison with ResNet-18 runs extending to 20 million steps at a fixed learning rate of 0.0001. These differ materially from the default 0.00025, linearly decaying Atari schedule in Table 2, which remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The network-depth, mini-batch-size, and objective-function analyses in Figures 5–7 and 9 remain unchanged. The replacement Figure 10 supplies benchmark learning curves without introducing a new controlled ablation or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Both Figure 10 captions report means and standard deviations across three random seeds. The other seed counts, 95% confidence intervals, and stratified-bootstrap reporting practices are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 10 replaces the 40-game learning curves with 54-game ResNet-18 results. For example, PPO finishes ahead on Amidar in v8, whereas SPO finishes ahead under v9's different settings. These are replacement results, not a same-setting performance improvement. Table 1 and the other empirical figures retain their results.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.2 and Theorem 4.3 relax delta_TV = sqrt(delta_KL/2) to delta_TV >= sqrt(delta_KL/2), with the corresponding proof inequality adjusted. This broadens the sufficient condition while retaining the conclusions and proof structure.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about SPO's first-order simplicity, probability-ratio control, competitive performance, and suitability for deeper networks.

C2.justification: The explanations of clipping failures, corrective gradients, network scaling, and alternative objectives are unchanged. No substantive limitation or interpretation of the replacement Atari results is added.

D1.justification: Figure 8 now explicitly identifies final performance with the default CNN, and Figure 10 specifies its encoder and fixed learning rate. The ResNet-18 footnote drops the statement about input/output adjustments. Table 2 and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The Queeney et al. reference moves across a page boundary without changing the referenced work.

P1.justification: Localized edits change the correspondence contact, shorten the acknowledgements and ResNet footnote, rename Appendix B, and clarify captions. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 10 is redrawn from eight rows of five panels to nine rows of six, with reordered games, changed scales, a ResNet-18 legend, and removed repeated axis labels. Figures 6 and 8 receive caption clarifications; the remaining displays retain their designs.

improvement.justification: The broader ResNet-18 comparison makes the existing deep-network claim easier to assess beyond v8's few showcased Atari examples, including weak results on MontezumaRevenge and Venture. Clearer experimental disclosures and the modest theoretical generalization also help. These gains are partly offset by removing the earlier CNN learning curves, supporting a limited net improvement.
